title: Slide Headlines That Make a Point (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Slide Headlines That Make a Point
slides.notes: Most slide headlines are labels like Overview or Pricing. They say what a slide is about, but not what it's saying. Let's change that.

slides.title: Labels make the audience do the work
bullets: "Q3 revenue beat target by a comfortable margin"
Prospects skim headlines on their phone
slides.notes: A label leaves people guessing, and some draw no conclusion at all. A headline that makes a point gives the chart a job: proving it.

slides.title: Ask "so what?" and write a sentence
bullets: Write a full sentence with a verb
Be specific, with figures you can back up
slides.notes: Ask what the audience should conclude, then say it in a short, specific sentence. "Onboarding now takes two days instead of five" beats "Onboarding time".

slides.title: The headlines alone should tell the story
bullets: "About us" → "We help mid-sized retailers cut stock write-offs"
"Pricing" → "One flat monthly fee, scaled to your number of stores"
"Next steps" → "A two-week pilot with three of your stores"
slides.notes: Read your headlines in order, as a list. In the rewritten sales deck, the right-hand column on its own is a complete pitch.

slides.title: Notes restate the headline, then explain
bullets: Headline: "Implementation takes four steps and about three weeks"
Notes: "Getting started takes about three weeks, in four steps."
The point lands twice: on screen and in their ears
slides.notes: When a deck becomes a narrated video, the notes become the voiceover. Open by restating the headline aloud, so viewers get the point twice.
